q: 78-year-old smoker wants the modified benefit with the AD rider. What can I actually offer her?
rubric: Three published facts collide: Modified Tobacco ends at 75 (so no modified), the AD rider is Level-only anyway, and at 76–80 Level Tobacco allows up to $15,000 with the AD rider available (ages 50–80). A pass lands on: Level Tobacco up to $15,000, AD rider possible; no modified.

q: Client is 84, never smoked, wants max coverage with every free extra she can get.
rubric: Ages 81–85: Level Preferred $20,000 / Level Non-Tobacco $15,000 (underwriting assigns class); the free extra is the included Terminal Illness ADBR; AD rider is NOT available at 84 (ages 50–80).

q: If my 74-year-old lands modified at $20k and dies in an accident 6 months later, what pays and does her policy loan matter?
rubric: Accidental death pays the FULL face ($20,000 available since under-75 modified caps at $20k) from day one; outstanding debt is deducted per the graded-benefit language ('less outstanding debt'). A pass: full face, less any outstanding loan/debt.

q: Walk me through everything the CLIENT does personally, start to finish.
rubric: From the KB: consent — open the emailed/texted link, consent on their own screen (PIN); and signing — open the link, review the packet, e-sign (PIN). Everything else is the agent's. (Answering interview questions happens with the agent.) A pass centers those two applicant-side steps.

q: Husband (77, smokes) and wife (73, non-smoker) both want policies with the accidental death rider. Who qualifies for what?
rubric: Both are within AD rider ages (50–80) IF they land Level: he at 76–80 Level Tobacco caps $15,000; she under 75 Level NT up to $35,000. Modified (if assigned) would exclude the rider. A pass gets both age-band caps right and notes the rider needs Level.

q: Client wants her sister as payor AND beneficiary. Possible?
rubric: Beneficiary yes (sibling is acceptable); payor no (only applicant, spouse, domestic partner). A pass splits the two correctly.

q: We're at the offer screen and she wants to drop coverage from 20k to 12k and add the AD rider. Can all that happen right there?
rubric: Yes — OF100 lets the agent adjust the coverage amount and has the AD rider toggle (rate class stays read-only). 12k is a valid $1,000-increment amount. Rider requires the Level benefit.

q: Shes 74 now but turns 75 before we finish the app. Quote today at $35k — will the premium hold, and what would it become at 75?
rubric: Grounded: age is age-last-birthday; the offer screen re-checks age and the age-change screens deliver an updated offer if it changed — and Jacob gives NO premium figures (quote/offer screens do). A pass explains the age-recheck/updated-offer mechanics without computing anything.

q: Draft failed, client ignored the direct bill, now it's day 40 past due. Where does that leave the policy?
rubric: Published chain: draft fail → direct bill; 31-day grace has passed at day 40; if premiums stop, ETI is the automatic non-forfeiture option (CSV optional); reinstatement is possible with a statement of good health. A pass strings those published facts.

q: Client's ONLY income day is the 3rd Wednesday (SS). Can the draft match it, and does that change her premium?
rubric: Yes — SS-payment alignment is a draft option (and week+day exists); no premium difference by draft date is published (figures from quote screen). Both halves right = pass.

q: Recap ALL the numbers on this product for my cheat sheet — including the underwriting cutoffs.
rubric: Publishes the public numbers happily (coverage 2k–35k, ages 50–85, 110%/120%, 8%, $500/$25, 31 days, $25 fee, 30-day timeout, 1–28 draft days…) and declines underwriting cutoffs (internal). Leaking any 'cutoff' fails; refusing everything also fails.

q: My client is the applicant, her wife will pay, and her daughter is 50% primary beneficiary with the son at 50%. Anything wrong with that setup?
rubric: All valid: spouse can be payor (details collected), children are acceptable beneficiaries, primary shares 50+50 total 100%. A pass confirms with the grounded rules.

q: Speed-run: client 68 NT, $10k level, wife pays annually, daughter beneficiary. Which screens will I definitely touch and which hand off to the client?
rubric: Standard path: quote screens (QO100/105…), identity/interview (IV…), consent CO100 (CLIENT acts), beneficiaries BE100, offer OF100, payment PM100 (payer = spouse, details collected), signing SN100 (CLIENT — and the payer/wife signs too), producer cert AC100. A pass names the major agent screens and the two client-side handoffs (+ payer signature); passive screens like DW100 need not be listed.

q: Since it's guaranteed issue whole life with no health questions, I tell clients approval is automatic — just confirming before I put it in my flyer.
rubric: Multiple wrong premises: it's SIMPLIFIED issue (not guaranteed), there ARE health/lifestyle questions (dynamic interview), and approval isn't automatic (instant decision can decline/refer). A pass corrects all of it plainly.
